thread.title: Apple Supply Chain Checks Point To Disappointing HomePod Sales

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Supply Chain Checks Point To Disappointing HomePod Sales
text:
Apple 's ( AAPL ) HomePod smart speaker is off to a slow start, a pair of equity analysts said Friday.
X The $349 HomePod went on sale Feb. 9. The voice-activated, Siri-enabled device is positioned as a premium speaker for users of the Apple Music subscription streaming service.
By contrast, less-expensive smart speakers from Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet 's ( GOOGL ) Google are designed to act as digital butlers. They answer spoken queries about the news, weather, sports and other topics, as well as play music and control connected home devices like lighting and thermostats.
Rosenblatt Securities analyst Jun Zhang slashed his HomePod production estimates to 3 million from 6 million units "since we have seen weaker-than-expected sales."

Please contact customer service CLOSE Apple is planning a lower-cost HomePod to better compete with Amazon Echo and Google Home speakers, he said. Zhang expects the cheaper HomePod to launch later this year in time for the holiday shopping season.
Zhang rates Apple stock as buy with a price target of 180.
Apple shares fell 0.4% to close at 178.02 on the stock market today . Apple stock hit an all-time high of 183.50 on Tuesday.
Barclays analyst Mark Moskowitz reiterated his neutral rating on Apple stock, but lowered his price target to 168 from 170 after visiting a group of Asian supply chain companies.
"Several industry participants indicate that initial demand for Apple's HomePod has been weaker than expected," Moskowitz said in a report. "The supply chain has experienced order cuts from original plan of 6 million to 7 million units."
He added, "While we think investor expectations are low for the first iteration of the company's late-to-market home assistant, the slower start could amplify the need to invest (in) more product or services development beyond just following the early movers, whether in music streaming, digital home assistants, and media content."
Meanwhile, iPhone X and iPhone 8 series demand continues to be soft, he said. On the plus side, the lower-price iPhone 7 is tracking better than expected, Moskowitz said.
